After some completions, its useful meaning changes to the number of prerequisites of `a` that have not yet been completed. A count of two means that two distinct obligations remain; knowing only whether the course has any prerequisites would lose the information needed after the first completion.

The master map connects the argument: `[a, b]` creates `b -> a`; outgoing lists locate the obligations a completion removes; remaining counts decide availability; a queue retains that availability until processing; the checkpoint keeps counts aligned with unfinished prerequisites; and the completed-course count distinguishes a finished graph from a blocked remainder.

quotes.text: The choice among available courses cannot invalidate a requirement: each chosen course already has no unfinished prerequisite.

For maintenance, removing an available course is legal because all its prerequisites are completed. Its outgoing edges describe exactly the obligations that this completion satisfies. Decrementing those destinations updates the counts correctly, without changing any unrelated count. Each destination newly reaching zero enters once; other available courses remain queued. Increasing `finished` records this one new completion. The checkpoint holds again after the whole dependent list is processed, rather than midway through it.

Counts never increase during this phase. A positive count crosses zero only once, and initially zero courses enter during initialization, so each course enters the queue at most once. No additional visited set is needed.

For termination, at most `numCourses` distinct courses can be removed. If all were removed, those legal steps establish a schedule. Otherwise the queue is empty with some courses unfinished. The checkpoint says each such course still has an unfinished prerequisite. The finite backward-following argument above then finds a cycle, so no full schedule is possible.
There are finitely many course identifiers. Some identifier must repeat, which exposes a cycle.
Each course on that cycle must wait for another course on the same cycle, so there can be no first completion there.

Group members cannot require one another, since any such edge would have marked its destination blocked. Each successful round completes at least one new course, so there are at most `V` successful rounds and at most one final failed round.
Each retained entry records a legal completion, so the earlier proof establishes the returned ordering.

answers.answer: V 是課程數，E 是 pairs 數。正文定義 Big O 為忽略固定倍數的成長上界；此 contract 把有界識別碼、counts、單 slot 讀寫、比較、counter 與 reference 操作視為固定工作，配置或複製 k slots 則與 k 成正比。deque 端點操作以固定 block 配置為有界工作的模型得到常數成本。list.append 有 resize，不能逐次無條件當 O(1)；正文以比例 spare room 與歷次容量的幾何和說明 d 次單項 append 合計 O(d)，稱 amortized constant。m 是成長時的 list size，C 為最終 capacity，r<1 為往回縮小的固定比例，S 是該段的幾何總和；d_b 是 b 的 dependents 數。建 V lists/counts O(V)，E pairs 造成 E 次計數更新與 append，各串 append 的 d_b 總和 E；scan V slots；每課至多一次入列/移除，每 edge 的 dependent list 至多訪一次，故主法 worst-case O(V+E)，cycle 提早停止也仍讀完初始 pairs。空間：外層 adjacency 與 V inner headers O(V)，E refs 加比例 spare capacity O(V+E)，counts V、deque≤V 加 block overhead、scalar variables O(1)；resize 新舊暫存仍同階，所以 peak auxiliary O(V+E)，排除輸入、無 recursion，Boolean output O(1)。若 queue 換 list.pop(0)，V 個初始可修者會移動 V(V−1)/2 refs，即平方成長。反覆掃描替代法每輪初始化/查課 O(V)，掃 E pairs O(E)，至多 V 個成功輪加一失敗輪，得到 O(V(V+E))；chain 每輪只放行一門，可維持重複工作。done、blocked、optional group≤V，前輪 buffer 釋放，peak auxiliary O(V)、Boolean O(1)，輸入 E pairs 排除。若輸出順序，至多 V 次 order append，追加 O(V) 時間，總時仍 O(V+E)；成功輸出 V refs 為 O(V)，排除該輸出的 auxiliary 仍 O(V+E)。失敗的 partial order≤V 屬暫存，回傳 [] 為常數。以上新成本概念與符號在正文內可由相鄰句與公式還原，未發現必需卻無法從正文還原的成本前提。

quotes.text: Let `V = numCourses` and `E = len(prerequisites)`. Big O describes an upper bound on growth, ignoring fixed multipliers; `O(V + E)` means work grows no faster than a constant times the number of courses plus pairs, under the following model. Reading or writing one list slot, comparing bounded integers, incrementing a counter, and moving or retaining one object reference are elementary constant-size operations. Course identifiers fit within 0 to 1999 and counts within 0 to 5000; treating these scalars as bounded units is appropriate for this contract. This is an operation-count model, not a statement that all Python instructions take identical physical time. Allocating or copying `k` slots costs proportional to `k`.

With `V` initially available courses, draining a list through `pop(0)` moves `(V - 1) + (V - 2) + ... + 1` references. Pairing the terms gives `V(V - 1)/2`, quadratic growth even with no prerequisite edges.

An endpoint operation changes an endpoint position and, at a block boundary, a fixed-size block connection; it does not shift all queued references. With fixed-size block allocation treated as bounded work, each queue endpoint operation has constant cost in this model, matching the documented approximately `O(1)` behavior.
A growth may copy the old references, so one append is not always constant work.

After growing a sufficiently large list of size `m`, proportional spare room allows at least a fixed fraction of `m` further single-item appends before another growth. Charge the cost proportional to `m` of that growth across those following appends; each receives only a constant charge. Equivalently, look backward from final capacity `C`: successive earlier growth sizes shrink by a fixed factor below one, apart from small sizes. Their copying work is bounded by `C + rC + r²C + ... = C/(1-r)` for some fixed `r < 1`. To see the bound, multiplying the sum by `r` leaves the original sum minus its first term; subtraction gives `(1-r)S = C`. Small initial capacities add fixed work. Final capacity is proportional to the final length, so `d` single-item appends, including their ordinary writes, take `O(d)` total work. This aggregate guarantee is called amortized constant time per append. It applies here because each adjacency list only grows by one appended item at a time; no alternating deletion or bulk update is being smuggled into the argument.

Building the `V` independent lists and `V` counts costs `O(V)`. Reading `E` pairs does `E` counter updates and `E` appends. If course `b` has `d_b` dependents, its append sequence costs `O(d_b)`; summing `d_b` across all courses gives exactly `E`. Small-list overhead contributes at most another `O(V)`. Building the representation therefore costs `O(V + E)`.

The readiness scan checks `V` slots and enqueues at most `V` courses. During processing, each course is enqueued and removed at most once. Each edge appears in exactly one dependent list, and that list is visited at most once. Hence all executions of the inner loop total at most `E`, even though the code nests that loop inside a `while`. Setup, queue operations and edge updates sum to worst-case `O(V + E)` time, with list construction analyzed over its append sequences. A cycle may stop processing early, but cannot avoid the initial pair-reading work.

For auxiliary space, the outer adjacency list and its inner-list headers use `O(V)` slots or fixed-size records. The inner lists retain `E` references plus spare capacity proportional to `V + E`, by the same growth policy. Counts use `V` scalar slots, and the queue holds at most `V` entries plus fixed-size block overhead proportional to that capacity. Scalar loop variables need constant space. A resize can temporarily keep old and new storage alive, but both have size proportional to the list being grown; this leaves the peak bound `O(V + E)`. The existing input is excluded from auxiliary space, and the returned Boolean is `O(1)` output space. No recursion stack is used.

Each successful round completes at least one new course, so there are at most `V` successful rounds and at most one final failed round. Initializing flags and inspecting courses costs `O(V)` per round; checking every pair costs `O(E)`. The resulting bound is `O(V(V + E))`. A length-`V` prerequisite chain releases only one course per round, showing why the repeated work can persist as size grows. `done`, `blocked` and an optional group buffer each hold at most `V` entries, so peak auxiliary storage is `O(V)`; old round buffers are released before the next round. The Boolean output stays `O(1)`. The input's `E` pairs remain live and are excluded under the same convention.

This adaptation adds at most `V` single-item appends to one growing list. The append-only argument still applies, so the added work is `O(V)` and the whole algorithm remains `O(V + E)`. The adjacency representation, counts and queue remain, so auxiliary storage excluding a successful returned order stays `O(V + E)`. Successful output contains exactly `V` references and takes `O(V)` output space. On failure, the partial order is temporary auxiliary storage of at most `V` entries and the returned empty list has constant size.

quotes.text: A different requirement changes what the main solution must retain: return one valid course order, or `[]` if impossible. Start an empty `order` list and append `course` immediately after each removal. Return `order` if its length equals `V`, otherwise return `[]`. Each retained entry records a legal completion, so the earlier proof establishes the returned ordering. No smallest-first guarantee follows from FIFO; for the movie, 4 appears before 1.

If storing another `E` references is unacceptable but the original pair list can be scanned repeatedly, there is a slower alternative. Keep `done[V]` Booleans. In each round, allocate a fresh `blocked[V]` array of false values. Scan every pair `[a, b]`; if both `a` and `b` are unfinished, set `blocked[a]` to true. Then identify all unfinished, unblocked courses and mark that whole group done only after the scan has finished. These are exactly the courses with no unfinished prerequisite at the start of that round. Stop successfully when all are done, or unsuccessfully when a round adds none.
The resulting bound is `O(V(V + E))`.
`done`, `blocked` and an optional group buffer each hold at most `V` entries, so peak auxiliary storage is `O(V)`; old round buffers are released before the next round.
